description: Eight voltage knobs, put out together as one polyphonic cable and one at a time as a sequence

params.text: Sets the voltage for its own step, over whatever span the range switch is set to
Sets how many of the eight knobs are used, both as the sequence length and as the number of polyphonic channels, 1 to 8
Sets the span the eight knobs cover: ±10V, ±5V, ±3V, ±2V, ±1V, 0 to 1V, 0 to 2V, 0 to 3V, 0 to 5V or 0 to 10V
Chooses whether the sequence runs forwards, backwards or jumps to a random step
Steps the sequence once, as a rising edge at the clock jack does
Sets the chance that an incoming clock pulse is acted on at all, 0 to 1

inputs.text: A rising edge steps the sequence on by one
With a monophonic cable, a rising edge sends the sequence back to its first step; with a polyphonic cable, a clock pulse or a button press copies that cable's channels into the eight knobs instead

outputs.text: Carries a 1ms pulse at 10V each time the sequence steps
Carries all the knobs at once as a polyphonic cable, one channel each, whatever the sequence is doing
Carries the voltage of the knob the sequence is on, held until it moves

notes: the polyphonic output carries the knobs at all times and needs no clock; only the sequenced output and the trigger jack depend on one
with a polyphonic cable in the reset jack the clock pulse is used for copying and the sequence does not step; a monophonic cable there leaves the clock to the sequence and resets it
the range switch rewrites the eight knobs' own limits, so a knob set past the new span is pulled back to it
Rack's randomise command moves only the eight voltage knobs and leaves the length, range, mode and probability alone

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
